source.locator: Equations (3)-(4), PDF page 11; historical k interpretation on PDF page 10
source.verified: Translated primary paper: rate proportional to enzyme amount and S/(S+k). Translator footnotes identify C*Phi with Vmax and equation (4) as a dimensionless fraction. Modern notation is explicitly a teaching interpretation. The lesson avoids a universal Km=dissociation-constant claim and states initial-rate/single-substrate limitations.

review_methods: Read exact saved JSON with UTF-8; inspected equations, controls, complete checks, explorations, limitations and provenance.
Opened and located relevant passages in all three primary sources.
Independently derived expectations with normalization/log2, two-key logistic softmax, and rational initial-rate arithmetic; no API calls or handwritten replacement page.
resolved_previous_findings: The fixed scan is labeled absolute substrate concentrations, not S/Km ratios.
Scan labels exactly match the computation [0.25,0.5,1,2,4,8] and use concentration units.
Historical equation transcription is labeled; modern Vmax and Km mapping is explained as teaching notation.
Km is given its operational half-rate meaning and explicitly is not generally identified with binding dissociation constant.
Finite-S plateau approach and line sweep bound S<=20 are described accurately.
limitations: Generic concentration and concentration/time units are a teaching choice; these are not measured 1913 experimental values or reproduced optical-rotation units.
Historical k arose from the paper's equilibrium treatment; the lesson's modern half-rate definition and general Km caveat keep that scope distinct.
At positive Vmax/Km, every finite legal S has v<Vmax; the line and scan approach the asymptote without reaching it.
Changing S changes the current-point readout; fixed scan rates depend on Km and Vmax, not the selected current S.

failures.name: independent_science_scan_units
failures.details: s_scan=[0.25,0.5,1,2,4,8] is absolute concentrations, yet scan label/title/meaning call it multiples of Km. At Km other than 1 the bars are mislabelled. Keep all computations and cases intact; relabel this fixed absolute scan consistently as substrate concentrations instead of relative multiples. The source maps historical k to modern Km as teaching notation; add a concise limitation that Km is not generally a binding dissociation constant.
